subject: Biotechnology
title: The $1000 Genome
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The $1000 Genome.

hook.text: The Human Genome Project cost $2.7 billion — today sequencing a genome costs under $200. Price collapse changed everything.

buildup.text: Illumina's sequencing-by-synthesis reads millions of DNA fragments simultaneously — massively parallel processing.

discovery.text: Cheaper sequencing democratized genomics — hospitals, startups, and even consumers can now read their DNA.

twist.text: Sequencing is cheap but interpretation is expensive — understanding what variants mean still requires expert analysis.

climax.text: Nanopore sequencing fits in your palm — the MinION reads DNA in real time, even in remote field locations.

punchline.text: Read a genome for the price of an MRI — sequencing is now routine medicine.

quiz.question: Why hasn't cheap genome sequencing immediately improved healthcare for everyone?
options: Most people do not have enough DNA to sequence
Interpreting what genetic variants mean still requires expensive expert analysis
Sequencing machines are too large for hospitals to install
